MINUTES

  SEPTEMBER 11, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by

Manager’s Office, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

City Council Members Present: Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Staff Present: City Manager Doug Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Senior Planner Jeannie Naughton

13.  CLOSED SESSION (TAKEN OUT OF ORDER)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Government Code §54957; Title: Succession Planning for Management, Professional,

meeting of the City Council beginning at 6:30 p.m. for the purpose of conducting interviews for
appointments to City Commissions/Committees.
At 7:00 p.m., the COUNCIL reconvened in open session in the City Council Chamber, 4045 Palos

 8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  PROPOSAL TO CONDUCT AN INITIAL STUDY AND MITIGATED NEGATIVE
  DECLARATION FOR THE NORRIS CENTER PAVILION EXPANSION – APPLICANT: PV
  PERFORMING ARTS; LOCATION: 501 INDIAN PEAK ROAD

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the contract with Michael Baker
  International, Inc. in the amount of $32,330 to prepare the Initial Study and resulting,
  appropriate environmental determination for the Norris Pavilion Expansion project.

  Senior Planner Naughton provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested that the Council consider reducing or
  waiving the City’s administrative fee given that Palos Verdes Performing Arts is a non-
  profit organization and provides a benefit to the community; and recognizing that Palos
  Verdes Performing Arts is the only non-profit with infrastructure operating in the City.

  Julie Moe Reynolds, PV Arts Center addressed the Council to explain the importance of
  the expansion in providing quality programs to the community.

  City Manager Prichard commented that the City has had a beneficial partnership with
  PV Arts over the years and the City has uses the facility for a minimal fee for several
  events each year.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AUTHORIZE THE CONTRACT WITH MICHAEL BAKER
  INTERNATIONAL, INC. IN THE AMOUNT OF $32,330 TO PREPARE THE INITIAL
  STUDY AND RESULTING APPROPRIATE ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION
  FOR THE NORRIS PAVILION EXPANSION PROJECT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  City Attorney Davis explained the circumstances under which the City would be allowed
  to waive the fees in this type of circumstance. Discussion ensued concerning the public
  benefit that PV Arts provides to the community through programs and services.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, City Manager Prichard reviewed the
  history of the property where the Norris Pavilion is located and the negotiation process
  that occurred when the City sold the property to PV Arts, including the agreement
  allowing the City to use the facility at no cost for rental.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL MAKE FINDINGS THAT PV PERFORMING
  ARTS/NORRIS THEATER PROVIDES PUBLIC BENEFIT IN THE AREA OF ARTS
  AND RECREATION THROUGH VARIOUS PROGRAMS AND WAIVE THE CITY’S
  21% ADMINISTRATIVE OVERHEAD CHARGE ON THE CONTRACT IN
  RECOGNITION OF THAT PUBLIC BENEFIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 11, 2018
 B.  RECOMMENDATION OF THE WASTE NEGOTIATIONS SUBCOMMITTEE AND AWARD
  THE EXCLUSIVE FRANCHISE AGREEMENT TO WASTE MANAGEMENT FOR
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL SOLID WASTE, RECYLCABLE MATERIALS AND
  ORGANIC WASTE COLLECTION SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Franchise Agreement for
  Residential and Commercial Solid Waste, Recyclable Materials and Organic Waste
  Collection Services between the City and Waste Management.

  Assistant to the City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Richard Tagore-Erwin, R3 Consulting provided an overview presentation of the
  negotiation process including the background of the agreement; new regulations; key
  terms of the agreement; and the commercial and residential rates.

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN, Assistant to the City Manager Davis
  noted that although the “bagster” program is not included in the City’s franchise
  agreement, residents will be able to take advantage of the program through local
  retailers and Waste Management will pick up the bags.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL regarding potential capital expenditures
  that Waste Management will be required to make during the term of the agreement, Mr.
  Tagore-Erwin stated that collection trucks will be replaced, residential containers will
  be in a replacement cycle; and new commercial collection containers will be necessary.

  Discussion ensued concerning the status of recyclable materials markets and the City’s
  rates as compared to rates in other Southern California cities. Further discussion
  ensued concerning the service level that the City receives and the additional value added
  services provided in the agreement.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL regarding the proposed rates and services,
  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN provided an overview the negotiation process and
  community outreach.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE FRANCHISE AGREEMENT
  RESIDENTIAL AND COMMERCIAL SOLID WASTE, RECYCLABLE MATERIALS
  AND ORGANIC WASTE COLLECTION SERVICES BETWEEN THE CITY AND
  WASTE MANAGEMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

NONE.

NONE.

SEPTEMBER 11, 2018
 11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information
  and reports to other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities
  of currently active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide
  governmental associations, special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their
  various committees on which Members of the City Council might serve or have an interest,
  which are not otherwise agendized.

  MAYOR HUFF mentioned that the SBCCOG annual report was received, which
  emphasized that they have completed each of the member cities’ climate action plans.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL updated the COUNCIL on the SCAG work program for the
  coming year.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL reminded everyone that the League Conference begins
  September 12 and that the City will be recognized with a Beacon Award.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on
  currently pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized
  for future consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

A.  APPOINTMENT OF A PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEMBER

  MAYOR HUFF reported that the COUNCIL conducted interviews over that last few weeks
  for an appointment to the Park & Activities Commission.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL suggested that consideration of an appointment of a Park &
  Activities Commission member be continued to the next meeting to allow additional time
  to consider the candidates.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

B.  APPOINTMENT OF A TRAFFIC & SAFETY COMMITTEE MEMBER

  MAYOR HUFF reported that the COUNCIL also conducted interviews over the last few
  weeks for an appointment to the Traffic & Safety Committee and Paula Boothe emerged as
  the top candidate.

  Following brief discussion, COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR
  PRO TEM MITCHELL

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPOINT PAULA BOOTHE TO SERVE ON THE
  TRAFFIC AND SAFETY COMMITTEE.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
SEPTEMBER 11, 2018
 C.  NEIGHBORHOOD WATCH LEADERSHIP GROUP MEETING UPDATE – MAYOR HUFF
  (VERBAL REPORT)

  MAYOR HUFF updated the COUNCIL regarding the Neighborhood Watch Leadership
  Group meeting held last week.

  City Manager Prichard noted that the scope of this group has expanded over the last
  several years to include areas outside normal Neighborhood Watch activities and
  suggested that the COUNCIL recognize this group as one to be included as one of the
  City Council committee assignments with annual appointment of a City Council liaison
  to the group.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL ACKNOWLEDGE MAYOR HUFF’S ROLE AS LIAISON
  TO THE NEIGHBORHOOD LEADERSHIP GROUP AND ESTABLISH THE
  POSITION AS ONE TO BE APPOINTED ANNUALLY AS PART OF CITY COUNCIL
  COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS.

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

OTHER MATTERS:

  MAYOR HUFF reminded the public of the upcoming City Celebration at the Empty
  Saddle Club and invited everyone to attend.

  MAYOR HUFF also mentioned that the Situational Awareness Seminar will be held on
  September 20, noting that information may be found on the City website.

D.  CORRESPONDENCE FROM CITY OF LOS ANGELES MAYOR ERIC GARCETTI

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
SEPTEMBER 11, 2018

F.  CORRESPONDENCE FROM ELI LIPMEN, DIRECTOR OF PROGRAMMING AND
  DEVELOPMENT, MOVE L.A. REGARDING TAKING A POSITION OF OPPOSITION TO
  PROPOSITION 6 – MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL provided background information on the request contained
  in correspondence from Eli Lipmen, Director of Programming and Development, MoveLA.
  Discussion ensued concerning the request.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  Hearing no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.
